title: Alloa Heritage Starter Pack
description: A curated, source-linked starter dataset for the Historic Town Explorer app. It contains detailed records for major Alloa heritage assets and non-spatial historical-development records requiring official geometry import or map digitisation.

project.name: Alloa
project.studyAreaNote: The app should obtain or let the user draw a project boundary; none is fabricated in this pack.

licensingAndAttribution.hesSpatialAttribution: Contains Historic Environment Scotland and OS data © Historic Environment Scotland and Crown Copyright and database right 2026, licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0.
licensingAndAttribution.warning: The records paraphrase source descriptions and link to source pages. Before commercial publication, confirm the terms for all council documents, historic-map imagery and any non-spatial descriptive text.

methodology.dateRule: A feature first appearing on a dated map must be described as 'present by' or 'first mapped', not as having been constructed in that year.
methodology.geometryRule: Null geometry is intentional where an official polygon/line has not yet been imported or a historic feature has not yet been digitised from a georeferenced map.
methodology.heatmapRule: Settlement age and surviving historic character must remain separate layers. The provisionalWeight field is suitable only for an initial interpretive heat map.

records.name: Alloa Tower
records.documentedDateText: 15th century, altered in the 16th, 17th and late 18th centuries
records.shortDescription: A major late-medieval tower house and the principal surviving element of the Erskine family's Alloa estate.
records.fullDescription: Historic Environment Scotland describes a 15th-century tower altered in the 16th, 17th and late 18th centuries. The tower is four storeys with an attic and is one of Alloa's most important surviving medieval structures.
